sn5.2:1.2: For Pasenadi’s wife of the same name, see [mn90:3.1]() and note.
sn5.2:2.3: “Two-inch wisdom” (_dvaṅgulapaññā_) is literally “two finger(-breadth’s) wisdom”. It is explained by the commentary as limited wisdom; or because women hold thread between two fingers. The subcommentary and the commentary to the Therīgāthā say it is because women test whether rice is cooked by pressing a grain between two fingers. Normally, _aṅgula_ with a number is a unit of length equal to the width of the middle finger, which is often a “small amount”. For example, the time past noon is measured when the sun’s shadow moves two inches ([pli-tv-kd22:1.10.16]()), which is the same distance the shadow moves each month (Arthaśāstra 2.20.42). Thus the first commentarial explanation is the most plausible: “two-inch wisdom” means “limited wisdom”.
sn5.2:2.4: It is Māra, not the Buddha, who doubts women’s capacity.
sn5.2:4.4: Gender categories apply in a limited sense to the realm of bodily conduct, but are entirely irrelevant when it comes to meditative immersion and wisdom.
sn5.2:5.1: Somā’s verses at [thig3.8]() lack this verse.
sn5.2:5.3: Read _asmīti_. Somā rejects not just the limited categories of binary gender, but any form of self identification.
